body.statement: Can the rank-adaptive spectral handle construct an estimator of \(\tau_{\omega}\) and a confidence interval with uniform asymptotic coverage over laws for which the smallest positive eigenvalue of \(H(X)\) approaches zero and the conditional rank changes on sets of positive probability, while reducing to \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\) on every fixed-rank separated law?
body.justification: Rank changes are the natural nonregular boundary of the proposed efficiency theory and cannot be hidden inside a fixed-rank assumption.
body.gap: Newey (2001) gives generalized-inverse optimality under a stable conditional system, while the staggered DiD and DDD literatures do not provide rank-adaptive inference for learned conditional weights.
body.consumer: A rank-adaptive procedure would prevent unstable standard errors when empirical clean-comparison scores are nearly redundant.
